newsitem.title: GERMANY: German media players bemoan Kirch loan plan.
newsitem.headline: German media players bemoan Kirch loan plan.

text.p: Politicians, leading media figures and the IG Medien trade union on Monday protested against plans to offer media mogul Leo Kirch a partly state-sponsored loan of at least several hundred million marks.
IG Medien deplored what it said were efforts to promote the development of a monopoly in the German media world and appealed to the Bavarian state government not to go ahead with the plans.

"A variety of opinions is the backbone of democratic society. Berlusconi in Italy has just recently demonstarted how dangerous an excess of power for one person can be in the media field," said Ruth Gruber, deputy head of IG Medien's Bavarian unit.

News broke earlier that Kirch was negotiating a credit line estimated at some one billion marks with a group of state-owned and commercial banks led by Landesanstalt fuer Aufbaufinanzierung (LfA), a bank controlled by the Bavarian state government.

Kirch, the owner of Europe's largest film library and what is estimated to be the world's twentieth largest media group, has run into difficulties of late in his bid to dominate digital pay television in Germany.
His DF1 digital station has attracted fewer than 30,000 customers, far off its goal of 200,000 by the end of 1996, while his spending on blockbuster film and sports events rights has soared.
Many in the German media resent Kirch's dogged efforts to win the war for pay digital TV, which have substantially pushed up prices for broadcast rights to big-ticket items.

"A regional government, which is supposed to stand for market forces, is supporting a big business which is aiming for a monopoly and therefore ruining all prices, for us as well," Jobst Plog, director of the Hamburg-based media group Norddeutscher Rundfunk, said in a radio interview.
"And if he (Kirch) fails, to an enormous degree, then the state government will come to his aid with public funds," Plog added.
Representatives of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) and Greens in Bavaria also spoke out against the loan plans.
However Alois Glueck, the Christian Democrat (CDU) parliamentary leader in the Bavarian regional parliament, defended the plans.
"Kirch is not only important as a media group for Munich and Bavaria, but also as a counterweight to Bertelsmann (a major Kirch rival)," Glueck said.
The LfA also defended the loan plans, noting that not only it was involved, but so too were "several large internationally active commercial banks."
"That alone shows that the business is being conducted according to regular market conditions and does not entail any state aid for the Kirch group," the LfA added.
